result.title: Distributed LLM Inference via Communication-Efficient Speculative Decoding
result.summary: Distributed speculative decoding has emerged as a promising approach for device--server collaborative large language model (LLM) inference, but its decoding speedup is often limited by the vocabulary-scale communication overhead. In existing distributed speculative decoding methods, exact rejection sampling requires transmitting full token distributions over the LLM vocabulary between the device and the server, which becomes costly in bandwidth-constrained environments. To address this issue, we propose DISCO, a communication-efficient framework for distributed speculative decoding, that eliminates vocabulary-scale distribution transfer while preserving the exact target distribution. DISCO achieves this by introducing a server-side replica of the draft small language model (SLM), which enables the server to locally obtain the draft-side distribution required for rejection sampling. As a result, DISCO exchanges only drafted token indices and scalar probability values between the device and the server. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that DISCO consistently achieves higher decoding speedup than existing distributed speculative decoding methods, particularly under stringent bandwidth constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DISCO，在端—云协同的分布式 speculative decoding 中，通过在服务端复制草稿小模型使拒绝采样可在本地完成，只需交换草稿 token 索引与标量概率，从而去掉词表级分布传输并保持精确目标分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 草稿—验证范式与「不传输完整分布仍保持精确性」的协议设计，可能为 latent 推理步骤的低成本草稿生成与验证、以及跨设备协同推理的通信开销提供核查线索，但其与视觉证据或推理状态无直接联系。
